title: The star forming cloud RCW 34
caption: The star-forming cloud RCW 34, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope
celestial: RCW 34 · constellation Vela · about 10000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A richly colored cloud of gas fills this picture. It is RCW 34, a place where new stars are forming, in the southern constellation of Vela, the Sails. The image was taken with the FORS instrument on ESO's Very Large Telescope in northern Chile.

RCW 34 is cataloged as an H II region. That name describes clouds of hydrogen gas lit up by hot, young stars. The energetic light from those stars knocks electrons off the hydrogen atoms, and when the atoms recapture them they give off a characteristic glow, strongest in red light.

Clouds like this are where stars begin. Dense pockets of gas and dust collapse under their own gravity, heat up and eventually ignite. Once the new stars shine, their light and winds start to reshape and clear the cloud that made them. The region is about 10,000 light-years away.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (7.23 x 7.36 arcminutes) and distance (10000 light years), the frame spans roughly 21 × 21 light-years. Its light set out about 10,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The VLT's FORS instrument captured this visible-light image through blue, visual, red and hydrogen-alpha filters. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: The telescope's long exposures and a filter tuned to glowing hydrogen reveal color and detail that would be far too faint for the eye.
